question: An arc of a circle with radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 2 radians at the center. Find the length of the arc.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Arc length is the product of the radius and the angle subtended at the center in radians.

Arc length = Radius × Angle (in radians)

Arc length = 14 × 2 = 28 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius (r) = 14 cm

Angle (θ) = 2 radians

**Formula Used:**

Arc length (l) = r × θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1670edbc03ec6762100ec1787a5c9ae0ba452fb6a4694998f2a06c48dceb1232.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Arc length (l) = Radius (r) × Angle in radians (θ)

⇒ l = 14 cm × 2

⇒ l = 28 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arc Length in Degrees

If the angle θ is given in degrees, the arc length l = (θ/360) × 2πr.

Area of Sector

The area of a sector is given by A = (1/2) × r² × θ (where θ is in radians) or A = (θ/360) × πr² (where θ is in degrees).

Radian to Degree Conversion

To convert radians to degrees, multiply by 180/π. To convert degrees to radians, multiply by π/180.</p
